newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just down as market consolidates.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just down as market consolidates.

text.p: Precious metal prices held most of their gains on Thursday from a blistering rally late the previous night.
Dealers said some profit-taking stopped progress for most of the metals with palladium particularly turned back from its 11-month high fix of $141.25 recorded at 0945 GMT.
"Gold is not out of the woods yet but we have seen a nice correction and some of the technicals have become more positive," a dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $343.65 per ounce, when April Comex was down $0.80 at $344.60, after $343.00 at its morning setting.
Dealers and analysts had been looking for a sharp correction in the sector for several days but when it came on Wednesday its virulence took some by surprise.
Now consolidation was expected. "It was too much of a shock yesterday to give back gains straight away," one dealer said, adding that business had been "manic" late on Wednesday.
He suggested gold might be looking to establish a trading range between Wednesday's price extremes of $337-$347 but other market professionals said gold could rise further.
"There is a lot of short covering mileage left in the market," said one analyst.
Andy Smith, precious metal markets analyst at Union Bank of Switzerland said the gold price appeared to be still lagging the other metals.
He said silver and palladium prices had both risen through their 200-day moving averages and platinum had topped its 50-day moving average.
"Gold is still nowhere near its 50-day ($359) so there is still a chance for it to rise," he said, adding that alternatively the market price "was telling us something."
Platinum was holding a premium of around $25 over gold compared with less the five dollars at the end of January.
"The whites (white metals) are racing away. There is all the ingredients of a change of sentiment," said Smith.
A platinum dealer described platinum's new premium over gold as "realistic".
"Platinum was due for a rally and has further to go," he said noting that platinum had been influenced until now by a gold price depressed by central bank and producer sales.

It was indicated at $366.50/$367.50 up $5.00 but off its earlier high of $369.50. Palladium also pared gains on profit-taking to $137.25/$138.25 barely changed, and silver was 25 cents firmer at $5.14/$5.16.
